objective: Native gluing of three-place knots builds surfaces (SURFACE-GLUING-20261024-001), and a native network is only a graph, which cannot fix a three-manifold. Ask what bits see once distinctions sit on the edges of a triangulation, each shared by every triangle around its edge, which makes them hubs. Hypothesis under test: among symmetric laws of bits on edges, one rule on triangles and one on tetrahedra, the only laws whose witness counts are three-manifold invariants are trivial ones and parity, which counts the mod-2 first cohomology; and the Fibonacci rule, which sees surfaces exactly, needs a negative weight to see a three-manifold. Nearest known work: Pachner moves, Dijkgraaf-Witten invariants for the group with two elements, Turaev-Viro invariants, and the sign problem of non-abelian string-nets. Standalone value: a census of bit laws invariant under the 2-3 and 1-4 moves, and a sign obstruction for the Fibonacci rule.
status: Complete 2026-10-24: dimension three through hubs. Native networks see only the dual graph (the sphere and L(4,1) share one); among 32,768 symmetric bit laws on edges only trivial and parity laws survive the 2-3 and 1-4 moves, so bits see a three-manifold only through hubs and then only through mod-2 first cohomology; the Fibonacci rule needs a negative weight (W10 = -(W9 t2)^2) to see three-manifolds. Next: a bounded scan on signed witnesses, deferred to the owner.
title: Dimension three through hubs: what bits see of a three-manifold
